name: The Palace Kitchen
summary: A round hearth with a tripod cauldron on it, a domed bread oven, querns and pots, and walls black with a century of smoke.
description: The palace eats well and this is why: a round clay hearth with a bronze tripod cauldron standing in the fire, a domed oven in the far corner baking bread for a household of two hundred, querns along the wall for the grinding, and pots and amphorae wherever there was room. The walls have not been ochre for a generation; the smoke has seen to that. Two fires burn here at all hours, so the kitchen is the brightest room in the ward and the most likely to catch.
build: Shell: the kit's InnerWard shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m plaster walls 4.00 m clear, 0.45 m fresco-blue capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 2.88 m centred on every wall.
Soot: a soot panel over the top 1.75 m of every wall section, below the capstone (the walls black from 2.2 m under the top).
Hearth (NW): a clay drum r 0.80 × 0.35 m at (−3.80, 3.80), three flame cones on it.
Tripod cauldron: a bronze tripod (legs 0.90 m, bowl r 0.30 m) standing on the hearth over the fire; its bowl at 1.79 m above ground.
Bread oven (NE): a clay dome r 0.90 → 0.25 m × 1.20 m at (4.20, 4.20); its mouth 0.50 × 0.35 m on the south face, dark.
Loaf table: cypress, 1.00 × 0.60 m, 0.80 m high, at (2.40, 4.90), two loaves on it.
Quern bench (SE): stone, 3.00 × 0.70 × 0.50 m against the south wall at x 3.60; a saddle quern 0.50 × 0.30 × 0.10 m at each end (x 2.50 and 4.70).
Pot bench (SW): clay, 0.70 × 3.00 × 0.50 m against the west wall at y −3.60; four soot-black cooking pots r 0.20 × 0.30 m on it at y −4.70, −4.10, −3.10, −2.50.
Amphorae: two, 0.62 m tall, on the floor at (−2.60, −4.80) and (−3.30, −4.90).
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.88 m (InnerWard), all open
Hearth NW and oven NE: both IGNIS sources, always lit

gameplay: The brightest room in the ward: two fires, always lit, so nobody hides here.
The tripod cauldron is loot, but it stands in the fire.
Hearth and oven are IGNIS sources; the soot-dry walls burn slowly, the amphorae of oil quickly.
